A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IRASim, with matching core architecture and original experiments despite the changed title and expanded scope. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments on RT-1, Bridge, and Language-Table, model-scaling experiments, and a human preference study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds RoboNet evaluation, LIBERO policy evaluation, simulated and real-robot planning, and robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The core frame-conditioned diffusion transformer remains, but v2 extends conditioning from one initial image to historical frames. It also introduces a planning procedure that generates outcomes for candidate trajectories and ranks them using predicted rewards or goal-image similarity (Section 4.3 and Appendix G), substantially extending the inference pipeline.

E1.justification: v2 adds RoboNet's multiple robot platforms, LIBERO bowl manipulation, Push-T planning, and real-robot drawer-closing and mandarin-placement tasks. Appendix A.4 also adds a physically implausible command scenario. The original three video-generation datasets remain.

E2.justification: The original VDM, LVDM, and Video-Ada comparisons remain. v2 adds MaskViT and iVideoGPT in the RoboNet comparison, GPC-RANK and GPC-RANK+OPT on Push-T, and random trajectory selection for real-robot planning. RoboNet comparator scores are explicitly attributed to prior work rather than new baseline runs.

E3.justification: New protocols include RoboNet prediction of ten frames from two context frames, paired evaluation of four policies in LIBERO and IRASim, and planning evaluation using IoU or task success. The new simulation applications use OpenSora initialization and expert plus post-trained rollouts. Original benchmark splits and short/long-trajectory settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds experiments varying planning candidates and post-trained rollout counts (Table 5), comparing planning cost functions (Table 6), testing one versus two context frames, and checking physically implausible trajectories (Appendix A). These extend the original conditioning comparisons and model-scaling analyses.

E5.justification: v2 adds repetition information: 50 runs per policy/evaluator, average Push-T IoU over 100 trials, and three repetitions of real-robot experiments. It also reports Pearson correlation. These concern new experiments; neither version provides confidence intervals, seed variability, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1-2 remain numerically unchanged as v2 Tables 1 and 3, but Figure 5 revises the Language-Table scaling curves. New results include RoboNet PSNR 24.6, policy-evaluation correlation 0.99, and Push-T IoU rising from 0.637 without planning to 0.961 with K=50 and P=1000. Tables 4-6 and Appendix A add substantial downstream and robustness findings.

T1.justification: Equation 1 generalizes the task definition to historical observations, and Equation 3 substantively revises the reverse-diffusion update coefficients. The diffusion loss and Appendix C conditioning equations remain unchanged; no new theoretical guarantees or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: v2's abstract and contributions add demonstrated policy-evaluation correlation, planning-based policy improvement, and test-time scaling, whereas v1 largely presented downstream policy benefits as prospective. The standalone IRASim Benchmark contribution and the explicit first-to-model-complex-7-DoF-actions priority claim are removed.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning failure-containing training rollouts, joint data/computation scaling, and why additional context frames may help little. Appendix G discusses cost-function failures and dependence on trajectory proposals. The conclusion drops v1's explicit hallucination and inflexible-resolution/action-space limitations while retaining the inference-speed limitation.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit action-vector conventions and RoboNet padding instructions, new comparator architecture/pretraining details, and documentation of rollout collection, reward modeling, and real-robot trajectory selection. Most original hyperparameter and hardware tables remain. The new applications are documented less completely than the original benchmark training.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused toward world-model planning and policy evaluation. v2 adds positioning around works such as Cosmos, Genie 2, FLIP, VLMPC, and GPC, expands its treatment of iVideoGPT, and removes several physical-simulator and DAgger references alongside the earlier 7-DoF priority claim.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Method exposition is condensed, experiments are reorganized into four application-oriented subsections, and appendix material is expanded and reordered. These are extensive narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a redesigned template with institutional logos, a boxed abstract, colored headings, and revised table/caption styling. It adds policy-evaluation, planning, RoboNet, and robustness displays, rearranges the architecture diagram, and relocates retained appendix figures. Figure 5 also changes the Language-Table axis and curves.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses a central gap in v1: the proposed usefulness of generated rollouts for evaluating and improving policies was largely untested. Paired LIBERO evaluation, Push-T planning ablations, and real-robot results provide substantial downstream validation (Tables 4-6). These gains outweigh reduced limitation disclosure and overstatement of consistent scaling, which Table 5's small reversals qualify. The new evidence remains limited by narrow task coverage and absent uncertainty intervals.
